title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
data_curation: Pre-training uses a 14.8T-token corpus with an increased math/programming ratio, multilingual coverage beyond English and Chinese, and a refined pipeline that minimizes redundancy while preserving diversity; document packing (no cross-sample attention mask) and a Fill-in-Middle (PSM) strategy applied at rate 0.1 are used, with a 128K-vocab byte-level BPE tokenizer. For post-training, 1.5M SFT instances span multiple domains. Reasoning data (math, code-competition, logic) is generated by an internal DeepSeek-R1 model: per-domain expert models (trained with SFT+RL) act as data generators, producing both <problem, original response> and <system prompt, problem, R1 response> samples, after which rejection sampling selects concise, high-quality data. Non-reasoning data (writing, role-play, simple QA) is generated by DeepSeek-V2.5 and verified by human annotators. The model-based reward model is trained from the V3 SFT checkpoint on preference data that includes the chain-of-thought leading to the reward, mitigating reward hacking.
curriculum: The pipeline is pre-training (14.8T tokens) then a two-stage long-context extension with YaRN (4K to 32K, then 32K to 128K, 1000 steps each) and finally post-training = SFT then RL on the base model. SFT runs 2 epochs with cosine-decay learning rate from 5e-6 to 1e-6, packing multiple samples per sequence with sample masking so examples stay isolated. R1 reasoning distillation is folded into the SFT stage via the expert-model-generated data, balancing accuracy and output length. RL (GRPO) then runs across coding, math, writing, role-play, and QA prompts. For general (non-verifiable) domains, RL feedback comes from self-rewarding / constitutional AI using DeepSeek-V3 voting. Post-training is remarkably cheap: only ~5K H800 GPU-hours vs 2.664M for pre-training.
method: The core post-training algorithm is Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), inherited from DeepSeek-V2: it drops the critic model and estimates the advantage from group rewards as A_i = (r_i - mean)/std, with a clipped policy-ratio objective and a KL penalty to a reference model (beta) and clip epsilon. Rewards come from a hybrid Reward Model: a rule-based RM (math final answer in a box, LeetCode compiler/test-case checks) for verifiable tasks and a model-based RM (free-form ground-truth matching, creative-writing feedback) trained from the V3 SFT checkpoint. The headline contribution is distilling long-Chain-of-Thought reasoning from a DeepSeek-R1 model into the standard V3: expert generators learn R1's reflection/verification patterns through RL with high-temperature sampling, and rejection-sampled outputs transfer that capability while controlling length. Self-rewarding via constitutional AI supplies feedback where rules are impractical. Pre-training adds an auxiliary-loss-free MoE balancing bias and a Multi-Token Prediction (depth 1) objective.
eval_metrics: Evaluated against DeepSeek-V2.5, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, LLaMA-3.1-405B, Claude-3.5-Sonnet-1022, and GPT-4o-0513 on MMLU/MMLU-Redux/MMLU-Pro (EM), DROP (3-shot F1), GPQA-Diamond (Pass@1), SimpleQA/C-SimpleQA, FRAMES, LongBench v2, IFEval, HumanEval-Mul, LiveCodeBench (Pass@1 and CoT), Codeforces (percentile), SWE-bench Verified (agentless), Aider, AIME 2024, MATH-500, CNMO 2024, C-Eval, CLUEWSC; open-ended via Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval 2.0 (length-controlled win rate) judged by GPT-4-Turbo; judgment via RewardBench. Headline: MMLU 88.5, MMLU-Pro 75.9, GPQA 59.1, AIME 2024 39.2, MATH-500 90.2, LiveCodeBench-CoT 40.5, Codeforces 51.6 percentile, SWE-bench Verified 42.0, Arena-Hard 85.5 (first open-source >85%), AlpacaEval 2.0 70.0, RewardBench 87.0 (89.6 with maj@6).
key_results: DeepSeek-V3 (671B-total/37B-active MoE) achieves AIME 2024 39.2 Pass@1, MATH-500 90.2 EM, and 85.5 win rate on Arena-Hard (first open-source model above 85%), competitive with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Full training costs only 2.788M H800 GPU-hours (~$5.576M), including just ~5K GPU-hours for post-training.
evolution_note: Building on DeepSeek-V2's MLA/DeepSeekMoE and GRPO recipe, V3 pioneers distilling long-CoT reasoning from the R1 series into a standard aligned MoE model via SFT/RL-generated data, anticipating the 2025 wave of distilling strong reasoning models into efficient base models. It also validates FP8 large-scale training and auxiliary-loss-free MoE balancing, pushing open-source efficiency and quality toward closed-source frontier models.
